report.summary: Reviewed chunk 7 of daedalus/eval/correctness.py: gate closure with verification, selection digest check, overlay application, test runs, and CLI main. Claims mostly kept, CLI docstring partly uncheckable.
risks: line 1702 | medium | apply_test_overlay is called before the test runs and its exception is caught, but if the overlay modifies the worktree and then the test run fails, the worktree is left in a modified state; the chunk does not show cleanup or rollback. | Check whether the caller (the gate wrapper) discards or resets the worktree after a failed run.

line 1748 | low | The CLI description claims 'never writes the primary checkout', but the chunk does not show the implementation of the worktree manager or the gate itself; the claim is uncheckable from this chunk. | Inspect the code that constructs the disposable worktree and the gate wrapper to confirm no primary checkout writes.

line 1749 | low | The --derive and --seed help texts say 'writes nothing', but the chunk only shows printing JSON; it does not prove that no other side effects occur (e.g., cache writes, logs). | Inspect derive_task_from_commit and seed_task_from_commit for any filesystem writes beyond printing.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: gate closure (verification, selection digest, overlay, test run, judgement) and CLI main.

symbols.name: correctness_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate closure that validates the task, checks before-state verification and revision, freezes the selection, applies a test overlay, runs tests, checks selection movement, and judges the after-state.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point. Handles --verify, --run, --derive, --seed, --task, --json. Prints JSON or human-readable output and returns exit codes.

claims.text: the task does not satisfy the schema
claims.why: The code calls validate_task(task) and if problems returns a refusal with that message.

claims.text: this task has no VERIFIED before-state. A FAIL_TO_PASS list that was never shown to fail on the base revision cannot certify anything. Run daedalus.eval.correctness --verify first.
claims.why: The code checks receipt.get("verified") and returns a refusal if falsy.

claims.text: the before-state was measured at {recorded} but this attempt is based on {base} -- a measurement of a tree that is not this one.
claims.why: The code compares recorded and base using startswith and returns a refusal if they do not match.

claims.text: THE SELECTION MAY NOT HAVE MOVED SINCE IT WAS VERIFIED.
claims.why: The code freezes the selection and later checks for movement after running tests.

claims.text: the before-state receipt declares no selection digest, so there is nothing to check the presented test lists against.
claims.why: The code checks if declared is empty and returns a refusal.

claims.text: The test set, the base revision and the gate configuration are fixed before a candidate runs and may not be re-derived, widened or narrowed afterwards.
claims.why: The code compares selection.digest to declared and refuses if they differ, enforcing immutability.

claims.text: correctness gate could not apply the test overlay
claims.why: The try/except catches any exception from apply_test_overlay and returns a refusal with that message.

claims.text: correctness gate could not run the tests
claims.why: The try/except catches any exception from _run_lists and returns a refusal with that message.
The code calls _check_selection and if moved returns a refusal with that message.

claims.text: Runs the repo's own pytest in a disposable worktree; makes no vendor call and never writes the primary checkout.
claims.why: The CLI description claims no vendor call and no primary checkout writes, but this chunk only shows argument parsing and dispatch; the actual worktree and runner implementation is not visible here.

claims.text: propose a candidate task from a fix commit (prints JSON, writes nothing)
claims.why: The help text claims 'writes nothing', but the chunk only shows printing; derive_task_from_commit is not defined in this chunk, so its side effects cannot be verified.

claims.text: derive AND measure a candidate task's before-state in a disposable worktree (prints JSON, writes nothing)
claims.why: Similar to --derive: seed_task_from_commit is not defined here, so the claim about writing nothing is uncheckable from this chunk.
The code filters tasks by id when --task is provided.

claims.text: the correctness corpus is empty -- nothing to evaluate
claims.why: The code checks if tasks is empty and prints that message.

claims.text: measure the BEFORE state of every corpus task
claims.why: The code calls verify_before_state(t) for each task in the --verify branch.

claims.text: evaluate every corpus task against its own reference fix
claims.why: The code calls run_corpus(tasks) in the --run branch.

observations.what: The gate refuses when the selection digest does not match the declared digest, but the message says 'may not be re-derived, widened or narrowed afterwards' -- the code only checks the digest, not whether the selection was actually widened or narrowed; a different selection with the same digest would pass.

The before-state receipt is used to construct BeforeState with f2p and p2p from the receipt, but the actual a_f2p and a_p2p are passed to judge_after_state; the receipt's f2p/p2p are not compared to the measured ones -- only the selection digest is checked.
The CLI --verify branch returns 1 if any row is not verified, but the message printed for unverified rows uses row['reasons'] which is populated by verify_before_state -- not visible in this chunk.
